The 59.5 dB low-frequency plateau is far below the specified AVOL (108 dB at 10 kOhm, 86 dB at 100 Ohm), so this curve is NOT the DC open-loop gain; it behaves like a closed-loop (or loop-gain test) response with 60 dB gain and a ~5 MHz pole (gain x bandwidth ~5 GHz). current_noise.curve_source: G20 'Input Referred Current Noise', p9; VS = +/-2.5 V, VCM = 0.25 V, TA = 25 C; linear axes 0-200 MHz and 0-15 pA/rtHz (axis label printed as 'rhoA/rtHz'); CURVE +/-0.2 pA/rtHz; noisy trace, looks measured (not labelled)
current_noise.hf_behavior: rising, approximately proportional to frequency (+20 dB/decade): ~0.07 pA/rtHz per MHz, i.e. 7 pA/rtHz at 100 MHz, 10 pA/rtHz at 150 MHz, 12 pA/rtHz at 190-200 MHz (slope flattens above ~180 MHz). The 7 fA/rtHz spot value at 100 kHz lies on the same line (7 pA x f/100 MHz), so the device has no flat shot-noise floor visible above 100 kHz.
current_noise.explanation_in_datasheet: None for the physical origin. p12 only states that in a TIA 'iN dominates at higher frequencies' (Figs 2-3) while 'at lower frequencies, the RF contribution dominates', and treats eN separately through the noise gain (1 + 2 pi RF CIN f).
current_noise.how_measured_or_defined: Spot value: 'input current noise density', TYP, not tested. G20: not stated whether measured or simulated; trace is noisy (measurement-like). Figs 2-3 (p13) breakdown curves are smooth model curves; their iN line is ~5.3 fA/rtHz at 107 kHz and ~5.1 pA/rtHz at 107 MHz, i.e. ~25 % below G20.

tia_content.what: TIA design equations: response RF/(1 + 2 zeta s/omega + s^2/omega^2); omega = sqrt(2 pi GBW/(RF (CIN + CF))); maximum TIA bandwidth fTIA = sqrt(GBW/(2 pi RF CIN)); zeta = 1/2 [ sqrt(1/(2 pi GBW RF (CIN + CF))) + RF (CF + (CIN + CF)/(1 + A0)) sqrt(2 pi GBW/(RF (CIN + CF))) ]; CF > sqrt(CIN/(pi GBW RF)) (CIN >> CF); decompensation requires CIN/CF >= 10

tia_content.R_F: 20 kOhm: CIN 1 pF -> 60/100 fF, CIN 5 pF -> 140/500 fF; 402 kOhm: CIN 1 pF -> 13/100 fF, CIN 5 pF -> 31/500 fF
tia_content.C_F: min from damping, max from CIN/CF >= 10

tia_content.what: RF thermal noise is the lesser low-frequency term when (eN/RF)/sqrt(4kT/RF) >= 1, i.e. RF < 860 Ohm for eN = 4.0 nV/rtHz

application_guidance: Layout: shield feedback-resistor E-field with a ground trace under the resistor (100 fF -> 11.6 fF, Fig 6); very sensitive to capacitive load (appreciable ringing above 5 pF, p16); guard ring using S8 NC pins (Fig 8); SOIC best for leakage; no ceramic capacitor or filter at the high-impedance node.
abs_max_and_input_protection: Supply 5.5 V; input voltage V- - 0.2 V to V+ + 0.2 V; input current +/-1 mA (Note 2: two series ESD diodes to each rail, centre node bootstrapped by a buffered copy of the input); SHDN current +/-1 mA; output current 135 mA continuous; junction 150 C; I-grade -40 to 85 C, H-grade -40 to 125 C. Differential input should NOT exceed 2.0 V; internal protection then conducts (keep < 1 mA) (p16-17).
other_notes: Inconsistencies: (1) G21 conditions not printed and its 60 dB plateau is not the specified AVOL; (2) G20 y-axis printed 'rhoA/rtHz' (pA); (3) Fig 3 label RF = 499 kOhm vs 402 kOhm in text/Table 1; (4) offset text +/-2.5 mV (PNP region, over T) vs table 3 mV over T; (5) ISC table typ 90 mA vs G15 ~118-155 mA; (6) 1/f corner stated 40 kHz vs curve; (7) TIA BW stated 210 MHz vs plot -3 dB ~220 MHz; (8) G22 legend 'AV = 10V/100V' means V/V; (9) Figs 2-3 model iN ~25 % below the G20 curve.
pages_read: All 22 PDF pages rendered at 160 dpi and read; G16, G17, G20, G21, G22, Figs 2-3 and both TIA responses re-rendered at 300 dpi and digitised. PDF page index = printed page number. Pages 18-21 are package drawings.
